quests.instruction: Say “bus” slowly: b-u-s. Where do you hear the /s/ sound?
quests.hint: Say the word and listen for the very last sound before you stop.
quests.explanation: “Bus” ends with the hissing /s/. The first sound is /b/ and the middle sound is /u/.
quests.funFact: Every word has a beginning, a middle and an end, and your ears can find sounds in all three places.

quests.instruction: Close your lips at the end of “gum” and hum. Which letter writes that last sound?
quests.hint: Your mouth is closed at the end of this word. Which letter hums with closed lips?
quests.explanation: “Gum” ends with /m/. The first sound is /g/ and the vowel /u/ is in the middle.

quests.instruction: Which word ends with the /p/ sound?
quests.hint: All three words start the same. Listen to how each one finishes. Which one ends with a puff of air through your lips?
quests.explanation: “Cup” ends with /p/. “Cub” ends with /b/ and “cut” ends with /t/.
quests.funFact: Cup, cub and cut only differ in their last sound. One small sound can change the whole word.

quests.instruction: Which letter spells the last sound in “bed”?
quests.hint: Say bed and feel where your tongue taps at the end. Is your voice still on?
quests.explanation: “Bed” ends with /d/. The b at the start is a different sound.

quests.instruction: The word “sun” ends with a sound you hum through your nose. Which letter spells it?
quests.hint: Your tongue tip touches the ridge behind your top teeth. Your lips stay open.
quests.explanation: “Sun” ends with /n/. If you closed your lips at the end, you would say “sum”.
quests.funFact: Sun and sum are two different words that only differ in their last sound.

quests.instruction: Which word ends with /g/?
quests.hint: Listen for the sound made at the back of your throat at the end.
quests.explanation: “Jug” ends with /g/. “Jam” ends with /m/ and “job” ends with /b/.

quests.instruction: Which word begins with /b/, a lip pop with your voice on?
quests.hint: Put a hand on your throat. For /b/ it buzzes. For /p/ it does not.
quests.explanation: “Bat” starts with the voiced /b/. “Pat” starts with /p/, which is only a puff of air, and “mat” starts with /m/.
quests.funFact: B and P are made the same way with your lips. The only difference is the buzz in your throat for /b/.

quests.instruction: Which letter is missing? _ear — it is a juicy yellow or green fruit.
quests.hint: Say the fruit’s name slowly. Do your lips make a puff of air or a buzzy pop?
quests.explanation: “Pear” starts with /p/. Changing the first sound gives you “bear” or “dear”, which are different words.

quests.instruction: Which word ends with /b/?
quests.hint: Close your lips at the end of the word and let your voice buzz.
quests.explanation: “Web” ends with /b/. “Wet” ends with /t/ and “wed” ends with /d/.

quests.instruction: Which word begins with /t/, a quick tongue tap with no voice?
quests.hint: Feel your throat. If it buzzes, the sound is /d/. If it stays quiet, the sound is /t/.
quests.explanation: “Ten” starts with /t/. “Den” starts with the voiced /d/, and “hen” starts with /h/.
quests.funFact: T and D are made in the same place: the tongue taps just behind the top teeth.

quests.instruction: Say “mud” and keep your voice on until the end. Which letter spells the last sound?
quests.hint: Your tongue taps behind your top teeth, just like in /t/. Is your voice on or off?
quests.explanation: “Mud” ends with /d/. A word like “mutt” would end with /t/, which has no buzz.

quests.instruction: Which word ends with /t/?
quests.hint: Finish the word with a quick tap and no buzz.
quests.explanation: “Pot” ends with /t/. “Pod” ends with /d/ and “pop” ends with /p/.

quests.instruction: Which word begins with the buzzing /v/ sound?
quests.hint: Put your teeth on your lip. Does your voice buzz at the start? Then it is /v/.
quests.explanation: “Van” starts with /v/ and “fan” starts with /f/. They are made the same way — only /v/ buzzes.
quests.funFact: Say fan and van with your fingers on your throat. Only van buzzes.

quests.instruction: Which word begins with /z/, the buzzing cousin of /s/?
quests.hint: Listen for a bee-like buzz at the beginning.
quests.explanation: “Zip” starts with /z/. “Sip” starts with the quiet hiss /s/, and “tip” starts with /t/.

quests.instruction: Which word ends with /f/?
quests.hint: Blow out a little air through your teeth and lip as you finish the word.
quests.explanation: “Puff” ends with /f/. Two f letters together still stand for one sound. “Pup” ends with /p/ and “pun” ends with /n/.

quests.instruction: Which word begins with /n/?
quests.hint: For /n/ your tongue lifts behind your teeth. For /m/ your lips close.
quests.explanation: “Nap” starts with /n/. “Map” starts with /m/ and “tap” starts with /t/.
quests.funFact: Both m and n are made with air coming through your nose. Pinch your nose while you say them and see what happens.

quests.instruction: Which word ends with /m/?
quests.hint: Press your lips together at the very end of the word.
quests.explanation: “Ham” ends with /m/. “Hat” ends with /t/ and “has” ends with /z/.

quests.instruction: Ham, jam and can are on the table. Which word ends with a different sound?
quests.hint: Listen to how each word finishes. Do your lips close at the end?
quests.explanation: “Ham” and “jam” both end with /m/, with closed lips. “Can” ends with /n/.

quests.instruction: Which word ends with the same sound as “drum”?
quests.hint: Listen to the end of drum. Your lips close. Which other word finishes with closed lips?
quests.explanation: “Drum” and “swim” both end with /m/. “Sun” ends with /n/ and “slip” ends with /p/.

quests.instruction: Which pair of words begins with the same sound?
quests.hint: Say each pair. Do the two first sounds feel the same in your mouth?
quests.explanation: “Kite” and “cup” both start with /k/, even though one uses K and the other uses C. “Gate” starts with /g/ and “tent” with /t/.
quests.funFact: Hard C and K make the same sound, which is why cat and kit both begin with /k/.

quests.instruction: Which word ends with the same sound as “bus”?
quests.hint: Bus ends with a hiss, not a buzz. Listen to the last sound of each word.
quests.explanation: “Bus” and “kiss” both end with /s/. “Buzz” ends with the buzzing /z/.
quests.funFact: Double letters like ss and zz still stand for just one sound.

quests.instruction: The word starts with /m/. Which letter completes it? _ap
quests.hint: Say the first sound of the word you want. Which letter makes the lip hum?
quests.explanation: The first sound is /m/, so M completes “map”. If you chose N, you would make “nap”, and T would make “tap”.
quests.funFact: Map, nap, tap and cap all share the ending -ap, so changing only the first letter makes a new word.

quests.instruction: The word ends with /g/. Which letter completes it? ju_
quests.hint: Say the word slowly and listen to the end. The sound comes from the back of your throat.
quests.explanation: “Jug” ends with /g/. B and D look similar to G when you write quickly, but they make different sounds.

quests.instruction: Which sound do you hear at the end of “top”?
quests.hint: Do not be fooled by the first sound. Say top slowly and stop at the very end.
quests.explanation: “Top” starts with /t/ but ends with /p/. A lip pop finishes the word.

quests.instruction: Where do you hear the /p/ sound in “pup”?
quests.hint: Say pup slowly and count each puff of air.
quests.explanation: “Pup” starts and ends with /p/. The vowel /u/ sits in the middle.
quests.funFact: Words like pup, pop and dad start and end with the same sound.

quests.instruction: Which word does NOT begin with /f/?
quests.hint: Say each word slowly. Two of them start with your teeth on your lip.
quests.explanation: “Fun” and “fin” start with /f/. “Bun” starts with the lip pop /b/.

quests.instruction: Which word does NOT end with /d/?
quests.hint: Listen to the very last sound of each word. Does your voice stay on?
quests.explanation: “Kid” and “lid” end with /d/. “Lit” ends with /t/, which has no voice.

quests.instruction: Which word begins with /p/ and ends with /n/?
quests.hint: Check two things: the first sound and the last sound.
quests.explanation: “Pin” starts with /p/ and ends with /n/. “Pit” ends with /t/, and “bin” starts with /b/.

quests.instruction: Which word begins with /v/ and ends with /t/?
quests.hint: Teeth on lip to start, tongue tap to finish. Say each choice slowly.
quests.explanation: “Vet” has /v/ at the start and /t/ at the end. “Wet” starts with /w/ and “pet” starts with /p/.
quests.funFact: A vet is short for veterinarian, an animal doctor.

quests.instruction: Which word ends with /n/ and begins with the same sound as “mop”?
quests.hint: Find the word that starts with a hum and ends with a hum through your nose.
quests.explanation: “Man” starts with /m/ like “mop” and ends with /n/. “Map” ends with /p/, and “tan” starts with /t/.
